name: Question 3
problem:
$$
P=[\begin{aligned}0.5 & 0.9 \\ 0.5 & 0.1\end{aligned}],\,q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]
$$

Given that $q$ is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix $P,$ what is the value of $a-b?$
worked_solution:
Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix $P$ is a stochastic vector $q$ such that 

$$
\begin{aligned}Pq & =q \\ Pq-q & =0 \\ Pq-Iq & =0 \\ (P-I)q & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $P-I,$ we get

$$
P-I=[\begin{aligned}0.5 & 0.9 \\ 0.5 & 0.1\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-0.5 & 0.9 \\ 0.5 & -0.9\end{aligned}].
$$

The matrix equation $(P-I)q=0$ is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix $M,$ which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}-0.5 & 0.9 & 0 \\ 0.5 & -0.9 & 0\end{aligned}] & {R}_{2} & :={R}_{2}+{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}-0.5 & 0.9 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the $1$st one). Thus, ${x}_{2}$ is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}-0.5{x}_{1}+0.9{x}_{2} & =0 \\ 5{x}_{1}-9{x}_{2} & =0 \\ {x}_{1} & =\frac{9}{5}{x}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the general solution is

$$
[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{5}{x}_{2} \\ {x}_{2}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}\in R.
$$

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to $1.$ Therefore, we have 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{5}{x}_{2}+{x}_{2} & =1 \\ \frac{14}{5}{x}_{2} & =1 \\ {x}_{2} & =\frac{5}{14}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
q=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}\frac{9}{14} \\ \frac{5}{14}\end{aligned}].
$$

Finally, $a-b=\frac{9}{14}-\frac{5}{14}=\frac{2}{7}.$

P=[0.50.90.50.1],q=[ab]

Given that q is the steady-state vector of the stochastic matrix P, what is the value of a−b?

a

Correct
EXPLANATION

Recall that a steady-state vector of a stochastic matrix P is a stochastic vector q such that

Pq=qPq−q=0Pq−Iq=0(P−I)q=0.

Computing P−I, we get

P−I=[0.50.90.50.1]−[1001]=[−0.50.90.5−0.9].

The matrix equation (P−I)q=0 is equivalent to the system of linear equations with the augmented matrix M, which we reduce to row echelon form using Gaussian elimination as follows:

M=[−0.50.900.5−0.90]R2:=R2+R1∼[−0.50.90000]

The reduced matrix above has one pivot column (the 1st one). Thus, x2 is a free variable. From the first equation, we obtain −0.5x1+0.9x2=05x1−9x2=0x1=95x2

Hence, the general solution is [95x2x2],x2∈R.

Since the steady-state vector must be stochastic, its entries should add up to 1. Therefore, we have

95x2+x2=1145x2=1x2=514.

Therefore,

q=[ab]=[914514].

Finally, a−b=914−514=27.
